title: scope_matches_path: literal bracket directories misrouted to glob matching
description: Codex review of sutra/238 (commit 5bfc110) found that scope_matches_path checks for glob metacharacters BEFORE attempting a literal match, so a scope naming a real directory that contains [ (e.g. src/app/[slug]/, standard in Next.js routing) is parsed as a character-class glob and matches nothing — reintroducing the silent-inert-constraint failure sutra/238 fixed, for bracket-literal paths. Fix: try the literal path-boundary match first, unconditionally; fall back to glob matching only when the literal match fails and the scope contains metacharacters (union semantics). Add tests for literal bracket directory scopes.
execution_record: Fix per codex recommendation: literal path-boundary match tried unconditionally first, glob fallback only when metacharacters present (union semantics — a scope can match both ways). Two new tests: literal bracket directory scopes (src/app/[slug]/) match literally; glob fallback still applies when literal fails. Full suite 1131 passed. Committed 9c0fddc on main (local, unpushed). Daemon redeploy needed again to pick this up — 5bfc110 was already reinstalled but 9c0fddc is not.
root_cause: scope_matches_path (introduced in 5bfc110) used glob-metacharacter presence as the dispatch condition — checked BEFORE any literal match attempt — so a scope naming a real directory containing [ was always parsed as a character-class glob and could never match its own literal path. The union case (a string that is both a plausible literal path and a glob) wasn't considered when the hybrid was designed as an either/or dispatch.
